attacks.claim: In dark mode, the text token resolves to near-white (#f2f2f7) while the day card keeps a hardcoded white background, so body text is roughly 1.1:1 contrast and the muted meta text is about 2.4:1. Both fail WCAG for about 30% of users.
attacks.evidence: --text: #f2f2f7 (dark) ... .day-card { background: #ffffff; color: var(--text); }

attacks.claim: The day-card background is hardcoded instead of using the surface token, so the redesigned core page renders as bright white cards on a black page in dark mode. This contradicts the claim that dark mode is supported since v5 and will be visible to every dark-mode user at 100% rollout.
attacks.evidence: --surface: #1c1c1e (dark) ... .day-card { background: #ffffff; ... } and ABSENT: any dark-mode QA; QA lists only 'Chrome 1440px (light), Safari iPhone 14 (light)'

attacks.claim: The mobile action bar is position:fixed at 72px tall, but .planner has no bottom padding or spacer, so the Sunday card (the last child) can sit under the bar and its tiles become unreachable at the end of the scroll.
attacks.evidence: .action-bar { position: fixed; left: 0; right: 0; bottom: 0; height: 72px; ... } and .planner { ... padding: 16px; ... } with 'Sunday is the last child of .planner'

attacks.claim: The most frequent planner action, adding a recipe's ingredients to the list (about 9.4 times per user per week), goes from a single tap to roughly five taps across three screens. The redesign adds friction to the highest-volume path, and 64% of these adds happen on mobile.
attacks.evidence: 'The old tile-level "+ List" button is removed to declutter tiles.' and 'tap the tile → recipe page → "Ingredients" tab → choose servings in the servings sheet → "Add to list" → toast with "Undo"'

attacks.claim: The flow relies on tapping the whole tile to open the recipe page, but the markup has no link or button for navigation. The tile is a plain li with an image, heading, and two buttons, so the core tap path and keyboard/screen-reader navigation to the recipe are unspecified and possibly broken.
attacks.evidence:
• Sheet-pan gnocchi

    25 min

attacks.claim: QA covers only light mode at 1440px and iPhone 14 width. It does not cover dark mode, the 360px width that is common on mobile (68% of sessions), or touch-based drag-and-drop, even though drag-to-move is the main new interaction and mobile is the majority of traffic.
attacks.evidence: 'Visual QA vs Figma: Chrome 1440px (light), Safari iPhone 14 (light) — pass' and 'Drag-and-drop between days ... VoiceOver: pass.' (no touch or dark-mode mention)

attacks.claim: The redesign ships to 100% of web users at once for a visual and interaction change that QA has not tested in dark mode or on touch. The watch list does not include layout, contrast, or drag-error signals, so a regression reaches everyone before it is detected.
attacks.evidence: 'Ship to 100% Tue 10:00 PT behind planner_v7' and 'Watch: planner page JS errors, shopping-list additions/WAU, planner bounce rate.'

attacks.claim: The stated goal of decluttering tiles is traded against the most-used action without a stated guard metric, such as per-recipe add-to-list conversion, so the net value is unproven.
attacks.evidence: 'Goals from the brief: less visual clutter on recipe cards' and 'Most frequent planner action: adding a planned recipe's ingredients to the shopping list (avg 9.4 times/week'

attacks.claim: The rollback claim says no data migration is needed because the API is the same, but drag-to-move and the new day structure may persist different state than the old planner expects. This is asserted, not shown.
attacks.evidence: 'old planner remains available by flipping the flag off (same API, no data migration).'

attacks.claim: Multiple identical 'Swap' buttons have no recipe-specific accessible name, unlike the overflow button, so screen-reader users hear the same label repeatedly without knowing which recipe each one affects.
attacks.evidence: <button class="btn-ghost">Swap</button> (repeated per tile) vs <button class="btn-icon" aria-label="More options for Sheet-pan gnocchi">

attacks.claim: Touch target sizes for the Swap and overflow buttons are not specified. Only .btn-primary has min-height 48px, so the other controls may fall below the minimum target size on mobile.
attacks.evidence: .btn-primary { ... min-height: 48px; ... } and no size rules for .btn-ghost or .btn-icon

attacks.claim: The fixed bottom bar does not account for iOS safe-area insets, so the home indicator may overlap the action buttons on notched iPhones. The bar's border is also rgba(0,0,0,.08), which is invisible on the dark surface.
attacks.evidence: .action-bar { ... height: 72px; padding: 12px 16px; ... border-top: 1px solid rgba(0,0,0,.08); } and no env(safe-area-inset-bottom)

attacks.claim: 'Generate shopping list' adds all planned recipes for the week with no stated idempotency. Repeated taps or re-generation could duplicate ingredients on the list.
attacks.evidence: '"Generate shopping list" (adds all planned recipes for the week)' with ABSENT: dedupe or idempotency behaviour

attacks.claim: The 'Share plan' action is listed without describing what data is exposed, to whom, or whether it creates a public link. The artifact does not address this.
attacks.evidence: <button class="btn-ghost">Share plan</button> and ABSENT: description of what 'Share plan' exposes or its link visibility

attacks.claim: The day card hardcodes a colour instead of using the theme token. This bypasses the dark-mode system and creates a second source of colour that future theme changes will miss.
attacks.evidence: .day-card { background: #ffffff; ... } alongside :root { --surface: #ffffff; ... }

attacks.claim: The nav element wraps only buttons, which is a semantic mismatch with the navigation landmark. Screen-reader users may hear a navigation region with no navigation links.
attacks.evidence: <nav class="action-bar"> <button class="btn-primary">Generate shopping list</button> <button class="btn-ghost">Share plan</button> </nav>

attacks.claim: Nothing material in the artifact beyond the unspecified Share plan behaviour, which is covered under privacy.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: no auth, input, or write-path changes described

attacks.claim: Nothing material. The change adds no new vendor, residency, or exit dependency.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: no new third-party services described

attacks.claim: Nothing material. Cards are capped at three tiles per day and images are lazy-loaded with fixed dimensions, which bounds growth.
attacks.evidence: 'Each day is a .day-card with up to 3 recipe tiles' and 'loading="lazy" with explicit width/height'

attacks.claim: Nothing material. No new compute, token, or per-request spend is introduced.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: no cost-bearing change described

attacks.claim: Nothing material for the artifact as written, apart from the Share plan question covered under privacy.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: no regulated data or platform policy change described

attacks.claim: Dark mode is broken for the day cards. The card background is hardcoded to white while text inherits the dark-mode light text color, so tile titles and content are nearly invisible for the ~30% of users on dark mode.
attacks.evidence: '.day-card { background: #ffffff; color: var(--text); ... }' with '@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { :root { --text: #f2f2f7; ... } }'

attacks.claim: In dark mode the muted metadata text on the hardcoded white card has roughly 2.4:1 contrast, which fails WCAG AA. The artifact's Lighthouse accessibility score of 100 does not cover this, since it was measured in light mode.
attacks.evidence: '.tile .meta { color: var(--muted); }' with dark '--muted: #a1a1a6' on 'background: #ffffff' card

attacks.claim: The fixed mobile action bar has no reserved bottom space in the page, so the last day (Sunday) and its tiles can be covered by the 72px bar when scrolled to the bottom.
attacks.evidence: '.action-bar { position: fixed; left: 0; right: 0; bottom: 0; height: 72px; ... }' and 'Sunday is the last child of .planner' with no padding-bottom or spacer on .planner or body

attacks.claim: Removing the tile-level '+ List' button turns the most frequent planner action (about 9.4 per user per week, 64% on mobile) into a six-step flow through a recipe page, a tab, and a servings sheet.
attacks.evidence: 'The old tile-level "+ List" button is removed to declutter tiles.' and 'tap the tile → recipe page → "Ingredients" tab → choose servings in the servings sheet → "Add to list" → toast'

attacks.claim: The redesign trades away the core action to address decluttering. The artifact's own usage data shows shopping-list addition is the dominant planner action, yet none of the stated goals (less clutter, at-a-glance view, action bar) address it, and no metric is set to protect it.
attacks.evidence: 'Most frequent planner action: adding a planned recipe's ingredients to the shopping list (avg 9.4 times/week' versus 'Goals from the brief: less visual clutter on recipe cards, clearer "this week at a glance"'

attacks.claim: 'Generate shopping list' is a one-tap bulk write for the whole week with no stated undo, confirmation, or deduplication. Undo is specified only for single-recipe adds, so repeated taps or re-generation could duplicate or overwrite list items with no defined recovery.
attacks.evidence: '"Generate shopping list" (adds all planned recipes for the week)' versus 'toast with "Undo"' defined only for the single-recipe flow

attacks.claim: The QA claims cover light mode only, but the release changes dark-mode rendering and ships to a population where about 30% use dark mode. The 'pass' verdict does not support a dark-mode claim.
attacks.evidence: 'Visual QA vs Figma: Chrome 1440px (light), Safari iPhone 14 (light) — pass, pixel diffs < 1%.'

attacks.claim: The release goes to 100% of web users at once with no staged ramp, and the watch list has no thresholds, alert owners, or rollback trigger. Given the unverified dark-mode and layout issues, a full-population launch carries avoidable blast radius.
attacks.evidence: 'Ship to 100% Tue 10:00 PT behind planner_v7' and 'Watch: planner page JS errors, shopping-list additions/WAU, planner bounce rate.'

attacks.claim: Mobile QA covers one device (iPhone 14, 390px) although 68% of sessions are on 360-414px widths. Android and 360px viewports are untested.
attacks.evidence: 'Safari iPhone 14 (light) — pass' versus '68% of sessions are on mobile (360-414px wide)'

attacks.claim: The rollback claim of 'same API, no data migration' is asserted without evidence. The new drag-between-days and per-slot structure may change how plan data is stored or ordered, and the flag's scope (per-user or global, cached client bundles) is not stated.
attacks.evidence: 'old planner remains available by flipping the flag off (same API, no data migration).'

attacks.claim: The 'Share plan' action is introduced with no specification of what is shared, whether the link is public, whether it expires, or whether it is revocable.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: any description of Share plan's data scope, link visibility, or expiry; only '"Share plan"' appears in the action bar markup and styles.

attacks.claim: Each tile's 'Swap' button has no recipe-specific accessible name, unlike the overflow button, so screen-reader users hearing a list of tiles get several identical 'Swap' buttons with no context.
attacks.evidence: '<button class="btn-ghost">Swap</button>' versus '<button class="btn-icon" aria-label="More options for Sheet-pan gnocchi">'

attacks.claim: Drag-and-drop behavior is unspecified when the target day already has a recipe in that meal slot or already has three tiles, so moves could silently overwrite or exceed the stated cap.
attacks.evidence: 'Each day is a .day-card with up to 3 recipe tiles (breakfast/lunch/dinner).' and 'Drag a recipe tile between days to move it.' with no collision rule

attacks.claim: In dark mode the day cards keep a hardcoded white background while text switches to a near-white token, so tile titles and metadata become nearly unreadable for the ~30% of users on dark OS settings.
attacks.evidence: .day-card { background: #ffffff; color: var(--text); ... } with @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) setting --text: #f2f2f7

attacks.claim: The fixed mobile action bar covers the bottom of the page, and the planner has no bottom padding to clear it, so Sunday's content can be hidden behind the bar on 360-414px screens.
attacks.evidence: .action-bar { position: fixed; left: 0; right: 0; bottom: 0; height: 72px; ... } and .planner { ... padding: 16px; ... } with "Sunday is the last child of .planner"

attacks.claim: Adding a recipe to the shopping list, the most frequent planner action and mostly done on mobile, goes from one tap to a six-step path, and the one-tap tile button is removed.
attacks.evidence: "tap the tile → recipe page → "Ingredients" tab → choose servings in the servings sheet → "Add to list" → toast" and "The old tile-level "+ List" button is removed"

attacks.claim: The redesign removes the shortcut for the top-used action (9.4/week) to declutter tiles, while the brief's own usage data says this is the action users rely on most. The proposal solves a visual goal at the cost of the core workflow.
attacks.evidence: "Most frequent planner action: adding a planned recipe's ingredients to the shopping list (avg 9.4 times/week per weekly-active user)." and "64% of shopping-list additions happen on mobile."

attacks.claim: QA covers only light mode and two devices at 1440px and iPhone 14. Nothing covers dark mode, which is the bug above, or the 360px-wide Android range that carries most mobile traffic, so the 'pass' claims don't support shipping to 100%.
attacks.evidence: "Chrome 1440px (light), Safari iPhone 14 (light) — pass, pixel diffs < 1%." and ABSENT: dark-mode QA, 360px viewport QA

attacks.claim: Every tile's 'Swap' button has the same visible label with no recipe name, so screen reader users navigating a list of up to 21 tiles can't tell which recipe each Swap affects. The overflow button has a per-recipe label, but Swap does not.
attacks.evidence: <button class="btn-ghost">Swap</button> versus <button class="btn-icon" aria-label="More options for Sheet-pan gnocchi">

attacks.claim: 'Generate shopping list' bulk-adds every planned recipe with no stated undo, dedupe, or handling of ingredients already on the list. The per-recipe path has undo, so this action is less reversible than the one it sits beside.
attacks.evidence: "Generate shopping list" (adds all planned recipes for the week) and ABSENT: undo or dedupe behavior for the bulk action

attacks.claim: Rollout goes to 100% at once with no staged canary and no thresholds or abort criteria for the watch metrics, so there is no defined point at which the team rolls back.
attacks.evidence: "Ship to 100% Tue 10:00 PT behind `planner_v7`" and "Watch: planner page JS errors, shopping-list additions/WAU, planner bounce rate."

attacks.claim: The watch list has no metric for the conversion of the new six-step add-to-list path, so a drop in the top action would not be detected by the stated guardrails.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: a shopping-list add-rate or per-path completion metric. Watch list is "shopping-list additions/WAU" only.

attacks.claim: The proposal adds a prominent 'Share plan' button but does not say what the shared link exposes, who can open it, or whether it expires.
attacks.evidence: "New sticky bottom bar on mobile with "Generate shopping list" ... and "Share plan"" and ABSENT: sharing scope, link visibility, or expiry

attacks.claim: The day card hardcodes #ffffff instead of using the surface token, which bypasses the theme system and causes the dark-mode contrast bug.
attacks.evidence: .day-card { background: #ffffff; ... } versus --surface defined in :root

attacks.claim: Drag-and-drop to move recipes is the main move path, but the proposal does not say whether touch drag works on mobile, where most sessions happen. The keyboard 'Move to…' menu is the only specified fallback.
attacks.evidence: "Drag a recipe tile between days to move it." and ABSENT: touch drag behavior on 360-414px screens
